skill.name: systematic-debugging
skill.description: A structured debugging methodology for software bugs, test failures, and unexpected behavior. It guides users through root cause investigation, pattern comparison, hypothesis testing, and verified fixes.
skill.summary: Guide debugging work from evidence gathering to verified root cause fixes.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

content.value_statement: Random fixes can hide the real cause of software defects and create new failures. This skill provides a disciplined process for tracing evidence, testing one hypothesis, and verifying the fix.
actual_capabilities: Guides users through four debugging phases from investigation to implementation.
Prioritizes root cause evidence before any fix proposal.
Shows how to trace bad values backward through call chains.
Encourages comparison with working examples in the same codebase.
Promotes one-hypothesis testing and verification before further changes.
Includes guidance for flaky tests, validation layers, and debugging instrumentation.
limitations: It is a methodology guide, not an automated debugger or test runner.
It depends on the user or assistant having access to project files and test output.
Examples must be adapted to each codebase and runtime environment.
It is not intended for broad exploratory code reading without a specific issue.

use_cases.title: Investigate Production Bugs
use_cases.description: Use a root cause workflow before patching a user-visible defect or service regression.

use_cases.title: Resolve Failing Tests
use_cases.description: Trace flaky or failing tests to the component, data path, or setup step that triggered them.

use_cases.title: Control AI Coding Sessions
use_cases.description: Keep Claude, Codex, or Claude Code focused on evidence before it edits code.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Root Cause Investigation
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a structured debugging path.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use systematic debugging on this issue. First read the error, identify reproduction steps, and list the evidence needed before proposing any fix.

prompt_templates.title: Trace a Bad Value
prompt_templates.prompt: Trace this bad value backward through the call chain. Show where it first becomes invalid, what evidence supports that, and which layer should validate it.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Broken and Working Paths
prompt_templates.prompt: Find a working example in this codebase that matches the failing path. Compare the inputs, configuration, dependencies, and control flow before suggesting one minimal change.

prompt_templates.title: Recover After Failed Fixes
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request after multiple unsuccessful attempts.
prompt_templates.prompt: We have tried several fixes and the issue remains. Stop further edits, reassess the architecture, summarize failed hypotheses, and propose the next evidence-gathering step.

output_examples.input: A test fails only in CI after a recent dependency update.
output_examples.output: The skill would produce a phased investigation plan: read the full failure, reproduce locally if possible, compare recent dependency changes, form one hypothesis, and verify it with the smallest change.

output_examples.input: A service writes files to the wrong directory during tests.
output_examples.output: The skill would trace the directory value backward from the failing write, identify the first invalid assignment, and recommend fixing the source plus adding validation layers.

output_examples.input: Two attempted fixes created new symptoms in nearby modules.
output_examples.output: The skill would pause new edits, list failed hypotheses, look for shared state or coupling, and ask whether the architecture needs a different approach.

best_practices: Capture the complete error message, stack trace, and reproduction steps before editing code.
Change one variable at a time so each test result can confirm or reject one hypothesis.
Fix the source of invalid data, then add validation at boundaries that could bypass it.
anti_patterns: Applying quick patches before proving the root cause.
Stacking several changes before running a focused verification step.
Treating repeated failed fixes as a reason to keep editing instead of reassessing the design.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps investigate bugs, test failures, and unexpected behavior through a structured root cause process.

faq.question: Can it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides debugging guidance. The user or assistant must run the needed commands in the local project.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it when an issue has a clear failure signal and you need evidence before editing code.

faq.question: When should I avoid it?
faq.answer: Avoid it for general code exploration when there is no bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior to investigate.

faq.question: How does it handle repeated failed fixes?
faq.answer: It recommends stopping after several failed attempts, reviewing the hypotheses, and checking for architecture problems.
